author: support@plugged.host

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# plugged.host — unified Minecraft: Java Edition installer
#
# Server Files: /mnt/server
#
# One egg, four server softwares. $MC_SOFTWARE selects the branch; the panel sets it
# from the type card the user picked on /create-server/{game}. It is user_editable
# (so the panel may supply a value at creation time) but not user_viewable, and
# StartupController refuses to edit non-viewable variables — so it can never drift
# out of sync with the files that were actually installed.
#
# Each branch is the official pelican-eggs script for that software. Every deviation
# below is forced by collapsing four eggs into one:
#
#   * One install container instead of four. installers:java_21 is Temurin 21 on
#     Ubuntu Noble and already ships curl, jq, git, unzip, zip and tar, so no branch
#     needs to apt-install anything at all.
#   * MINECRAFT_VERSION is bridged to MC_VERSION, the name the upstream fabric, forge
#     and neoforge scripts read. This egg exposes MINECRAFT_VERSION to stay consistent
#     with the panel's existing Minecraft egg.
#   * The neoforge branch reads maven-metadata.xml with grep/sed instead of `xq`,
#     which this image does not carry.
#   * forge and neoforge both symlink unix_args.txt into the server root — that is
#     upstream behaviour, and it is what lets one startup command serve both.
#
# Known limitation: Forge installers for Minecraft older than 1.17 predate the module
# system and frequently refuse to run under Java 21. Those versions are not offered by
# the storefront; the forge branch reports that cause explicitly rather than leaving a
# half-installed server behind.

set -o pipefail

SOFTWARE="$(echo "${MC_SOFTWARE:-purpur}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | tr -d ' ')"

# Upstream reads MC_VERSION, this egg exposes MINECRAFT_VERSION. Bridge once, here.
MC_VERSION="$(echo "${MINECRAFT_VERSION:-latest}" | tr -d ' ')"
BUILD_NUMBER="$(echo "${BUILD_NUMBER:-latest}" | tr -d ' ')"
SERVER_JARFILE="${SERVER_JARFILE:-server.jar}"

# Add .jar when SERVER_JARFILE does not already end in it
if [[ ! $SERVER_JARFILE = *.jar ]]; then
  SERVER_JARFILE="${SERVER_JARFILE}.jar"
fi

mkdir -p /mnt/server
cd /mnt/server || exit 1

echo "==============================================="
echo " plugged.host Minecraft: Java Edition installer"
echo " software: ${SOFTWARE}"
echo " version:  ${MC_VERSION}"
echo " jarfile:  ${SERVER_JARFILE}"
echo "==============================================="

# Wings rewrites server-ip and server-port into server.properties on boot, so give it
# a file to rewrite. Every branch gets one; upstream only purpur does this.
default_server_properties() {
  if [[ -f server.properties ]]; then
    return
  fi

  echo "Downloading default server.properties"
  curl -fsSL -o server.properties.tmp \
    https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pelican-eggs/minecraft/main/java/server.properties \
    && mv server.properties.tmp server.properties \
    || {
      echo "Could not fetch a default server.properties; the server will generate one on first boot."
      rm -f server.properties.tmp
    }
}

# Purpur only publishes builds for Minecraft 1.14.1 and newer. Older versions fall
# back to Paper, which covers back to 1.7.10 — the storefront markets this tile as
# "Vanilla / Paper / Spigot / Purpur", so either jar is a legitimate fulfilment.
needs_paper() {
  local v="$1" minor patch

  # Minecraft renumbered from 1.21.x to 26.x, so anything not starting "1." is newer
  # than 1.14.1 by definition.
  [[ $v != 1.* ]] && return 1

  minor=$(echo "$v" | cut -d. -f2)
  patch=$(echo "$v" | cut -d. -f3)

  # Strip pre-release/snapshot suffixes, e.g. "1.13.2-pre1"
  minor=${minor%%[!0-9]*}
  patch=${patch%%[!0-9]*}

  [[ -z $minor ]] && return 1
  [[ -z $patch ]] && patch=0

  # Older than 1.14.1
  if (( minor < 14 )) || { (( minor == 14 )) && (( patch < 1 )); }; then
    return 0
  fi

  return 1
}

install_paper() {
  local api data url jar_name

  echo "Purpur has no builds for Minecraft ${MC_VERSION} (its oldest is 1.14.1). Installing Paper instead."

  api="https://fill.papermc.io/v3/projects/paper/versions/${MC_VERSION}/builds/latest"
  data=$(curl -sSL -H "User-Agent: plugged.host-egg/1.0 (support@plugged.host)" "$api")

  url=$(printf '%s' "$data" | jq -r '.downloads["server:default"].url // empty')
  jar_name=$(printf '%s' "$data" | jq -r '.downloads["server:default"].name // empty')

  if [[ -z $url ]]; then
    echo "No Paper build is available for Minecraft ${MC_VERSION}."
    exit 2
  fi

  echo "Paper build: ${jar_name}"

  if [[ -f ${SERVER_JARFILE} ]]; then
    mv -f "${SERVER_JARFILE}" "${SERVER_JARFILE}.old"
  fi

  curl -fsSL -o "${SERVER_JARFILE}" "$url" || {
    echo "Failed to download Paper for Minecraft ${MC_VERSION}."
    exit 2
  }

  echo "Paper for Minecraft ${MC_VERSION} installed as ${SERVER_JARFILE}."
}

install_purpur() {
  local project=purpur ver_exists latest_version build_exists latest_build jar_name download_url

  # Resolve "latest" up front so the Paper cutoff check compares a real version.
  if [[ -z $MC_VERSION ]] || [[ $MC_VERSION == "latest" ]]; then
    MC_VERSION=$(curl -s "https://api.purpurmc.org/v2/${project}" | jq -r '.versions' | jq -r '.[-1]')
    echo "Resolved latest Purpur version: ${MC_VERSION}"
  fi

  if needs_paper "$MC_VERSION"; then
    install_paper
    return
  fi

  ver_exists=$(curl -s "https://api.purpurmc.org/v2/${project}" | jq -r --arg VERSION "$MC_VERSION" '.versions[] | contains($VERSION)' | grep true)
  latest_version=$(curl -s "https://api.purpurmc.org/v2/${project}" | jq -r '.versions' | jq -r '.[-1]')

  if [[ "${ver_exists}" == "true" ]]; then
    echo "Version is valid. Using version ${MC_VERSION}"
  else
    echo "Using the latest ${project} version"
    MC_VERSION=${latest_version}
  fi

  build_exists=$(curl -s "https://api.purpurmc.org/v2/${project}/${MC_VERSION}" | jq -r --arg BUILD "$BUILD_NUMBER" '.builds.all | tostring | contains($BUILD)' | grep true)
  latest_build=$(curl -s "https://api.purpurmc.org/v2/${project}/${MC_VERSION}" | jq -r '.builds.latest')

  if [[ "${build_exists}" == "true" ]]; then
    echo "Build is valid for version ${MC_VERSION}. Using build ${BUILD_NUMBER}"
  else
    echo "Using the latest ${project} build for version ${MC_VERSION}"
    BUILD_NUMBER=${latest_build}
  fi

  jar_name=${project}-${MC_VERSION}-${BUILD_NUMBER}.jar
  download_url=https://api.purpurmc.org/v2/${project}/${MC_VERSION}/${BUILD_NUMBER}/download

  echo "MC version:   ${MC_VERSION}"
  echo "Build:        ${BUILD_NUMBER}"
  echo "Upstream jar: ${jar_name}"

  if [[ -f ${SERVER_JARFILE} ]]; then
    mv -f "${SERVER_JARFILE}" "${SERVER_JARFILE}.old"
  fi

  curl -fsSL -o "${SERVER_JARFILE}" "${download_url}" || {
    echo "Failed to download Purpur ${MC_VERSION} build ${BUILD_NUMBER}."
    exit 2
  }

  echo "Purpur ${MC_VERSION} build ${BUILD_NUMBER} installed as ${SERVER_JARFILE}."
}

install_fabric() {
  local fabric_version loader_version

  if [[ -z "$MC_VERSION" ]] || [[ "$MC_VERSION" == "latest" ]]; then
    MC_VERSION=$(curl -sSL https://meta.fabricmc.net/v2/versions/game | jq -r '.[] | select(.stable== true )|.version' | head -n1)
  elif [[ "$MC_VERSION" == "snapshot" ]]; then
    MC_VERSION=$(curl -sSL https://meta.fabricmc.net/v2/versions/game | jq -r '.[] | select(.stable== false )|.version' | head -n1)
  fi

  fabric_version=$(curl -sSL https://meta.fabricmc.net/v2/versions/installer | jq -r '.[0].version')
  loader_version=$(curl -sSL https://meta.fabricmc.net/v2/versions/loader | jq -r '.[] | select(.stable== true )|.version' | head -n1)

  echo "Minecraft version:  ${MC_VERSION}"
  echo "Fabric installer:   ${fabric_version}"
  echo "Fabric loader:      ${loader_version}"

  curl -fsSL -o fabric-installer.jar \
    "https://maven.fabricmc.net/net/fabricmc/fabric-installer/${fabric_version}/fabric-installer-${fabric_version}.jar" || {
      echo "Failed to download the Fabric installer."
      exit 2
    }

  java -jar fabric-installer.jar server -mcversion "$MC_VERSION" -loader "$loader_version" -downloadMinecraft || {
    echo "Fabric install failed for Minecraft ${MC_VERSION} with loader ${loader_version}."
    exit 3
  }

  # The installer leaves the vanilla jar as server.jar and its own launcher as
  # fabric-server-launch.jar. Move vanilla aside first, then put the launcher where
  # the startup command looks for it.
  mv -f server.jar minecraft-server.jar
  mv -f fabric-server-launch.jar "$SERVER_JARFILE"
  echo "serverJar=minecraft-server.jar" > fabric-server-launcher.properties
  rm -f fabric-installer.jar

  echo "Fabric ${loader_version} for Minecraft ${MC_VERSION} installed as ${SERVER_JARFILE}."
}

install_forge() {
  local json_data build_type file_site version_key forge_jar download_link

  # FORGE_VERSION is deliberately not an egg variable — the storefront always wants the
  # promoted build for the chosen Minecraft version. The branch stays for parity with
  # upstream, and is the pin point if that ever changes.
  FORGE_VERSION="$(echo "${FORGE_VERSION:-}" | tr -d ' ')"

  if [[ -n ${FORGE_VERSION} ]]; then
    download_link=https://maven.minecraftforge.net/net/minecraftforge/forge/${FORGE_VERSION}/forge-${FORGE_VERSION}
    forge_jar=forge-${FORGE_VERSION}*.jar
  else
    json_data=$(curl -sSL https://files.minecraftforge.net/maven/net/minecraftforge/forge/promotions_slim.json)

    if [[ "${MC_VERSION}" == "latest" ]] || [[ -z "${MC_VERSION}" ]]; then
      echo "Getting the latest version of Forge."
      MC_VERSION=$(echo -e "${json_data}" | jq -r '.promos | del(."latest-1.7.10") | del(."1.7.10-latest-1.7.10") | to_entries[] | .key | select(contains("latest")) | split("-")[0]' | sort -t. -k 1,1n -k 2,2n -k 3,3n -k 4,4n | tail -1)
      build_type=latest
    fi

    if [[ "${build_type}" != "recommended" ]] && [[ "${build_type}" != "latest" ]]; then
      build_type=recommended
    fi

    echo "Minecraft version: ${MC_VERSION}"
    echo "Build type:        ${build_type}"

    file_site=https://maven.minecraftforge.net/net/minecraftforge/forge/
    version_key=$(echo -e "${json_data}" | jq -r --arg MC_VERSION "${MC_VERSION}" --arg BUILD_TYPE "${build_type}" '.promos | del(."latest-1.7.10") | del(."1.7.10-latest-1.7.10") | to_entries[] | .key | select(contains($MC_VERSION)) | select(contains($BUILD_TYPE))')

    if [[ "${version_key}" == "" ]] && [[ "${build_type}" == "recommended" ]]; then
      echo "Dropping back to latest from recommended: there is no recommended Forge build for the Minecraft version requested."
      version_key=$(echo -e "${json_data}" | jq -r --arg MC_VERSION "${MC_VERSION}" '.promos | del(."latest-1.7.10") | del(."1.7.10-latest-1.7.10") | to_entries[] | .key | select(contains($MC_VERSION)) | select(contains("latest"))')
    fi

    if [[ "${version_key}" == "" ]] || [[ "${version_key}" == "null" ]]; then
      echo "The install failed because there is no valid version of Forge for the version of Minecraft selected."
      exit 1
    fi

    FORGE_VERSION=$(echo -e "${json_data}" | jq -r --arg VERSION_KEY "$version_key" '.promos | .[$VERSION_KEY]')

    if [[ "${MC_VERSION}" == "1.7.10" ]] || [[ "${MC_VERSION}" == "1.8.9" ]]; then
      download_link=${file_site}${MC_VERSION}-${FORGE_VERSION}-${MC_VERSION}/forge-${MC_VERSION}-${FORGE_VERSION}-${MC_VERSION}
      forge_jar=forge-${MC_VERSION}-${FORGE_VERSION}-${MC_VERSION}.jar

      if [[ "${MC_VERSION}" == "1.7.10" ]]; then
        forge_jar=forge-${MC_VERSION}-${FORGE_VERSION}-${MC_VERSION}-universal.jar
      fi
    else
      download_link=${file_site}${MC_VERSION}-${FORGE_VERSION}/forge-${MC_VERSION}-${FORGE_VERSION}
      forge_jar=forge-${MC_VERSION}-${FORGE_VERSION}.jar
    fi
  fi

  echo "Downloading Forge version ${FORGE_VERSION}"
  echo "Download link is ${download_link}"

  if ! curl --output /dev/null --silent --head --fail "${download_link}-installer.jar"; then
    echo "Installer link is invalid. Exiting now."
    exit 2
  fi

  curl -sS -o installer.jar "${download_link}-installer.jar"

  if [[ ! -f ./installer.jar ]]; then
    echo "!!! Error downloading Forge version ${FORGE_VERSION} !!!"
    exit 3
  fi

  # Delete args to support downgrading/upgrading
  rm -rf libraries/net/minecraftforge/forge
  rm -f unix_args.txt

  echo "Installing Forge server."
  java -jar installer.jar --installServer || {
    echo ""
    echo "Install failed using Forge version ${FORGE_VERSION} and Minecraft version ${MC_VERSION}."
    echo "If the server has an unlimited (0) memory value, raise the default install resource limits in the Wings config, or set an explicit memory value in the server's Build Configuration — otherwise the Forge installer has no memory to work with."
    echo "Note also that Forge installers for Minecraft older than 1.17 often cannot run under the Java 21 this egg installs with."
    exit 4
  }

  # Modern Forge ships JPMS args instead of a runnable jar, and the installer writes
  # them under libraries/. Detect by looking for the file the installer actually
  # produced rather than by pattern-matching the version: Minecraft renumbered from
  # 1.21.x straight to 26.x, so any "is this 1.17+" regex silently stops matching.
  #
  # Note the args may reference a shim jar (26.2 ships
  # "-jar forge-26.2-65.1.2-shim.jar"), which lives beside them in libraries/. The
  # symlink alone is not enough in that case — see below.
  local args_src
  args_src=$(find libraries/net/minecraftforge/forge -name unix_args.txt -print -quit 2>/dev/null)

  if [[ -n $args_src ]]; then
    echo "Forge JPMS args found. Wiring up unix_args.txt."
    ln -sf "$args_src" unix_args.txt

    # A shim jar is referenced by bare filename, so java resolves it relative to the
    # server root — where it does not exist. Link it next to the startup command.
    local shim
    shim=$(grep -oE '[^ ]+-shim\.jar' unix_args.txt 2>/dev/null | head -n1)

    if [[ -n $shim ]]; then
      local shim_src
      shim_src=$(find libraries/net/minecraftforge/forge -name "$shim" -print -quit 2>/dev/null)

      if [[ -n $shim_src ]]; then
        echo "Linking Forge shim jar ${shim} into the server root."
        ln -sf "$shim_src" "$shim"
      else
        echo "WARNING: unix_args.txt references ${shim} but it was not found under libraries/."
      fi
    fi
  elif [[ -n $forge_jar ]] && compgen -G "$forge_jar" > /dev/null; then
    # Older Forge ships a runnable jar; the startup command falls back to it.
    echo "No JPMS args produced. Using the shipped Forge jar."
    mv -f $forge_jar "$SERVER_JARFILE"
  else
    echo "Install failed: the Forge installer produced neither unix_args.txt nor a runnable jar."
    exit 5
  fi

  echo "Deleting installer.jar file."
  rm -rf installer.jar
}

install_neoforge() {
  local xml_data artifact_name repo_url version_key neo_release neoforge_old download_link

  # As with Forge, NEOFORGE_VERSION is not an egg variable; the Maven metadata picks
  # the newest build for the chosen Minecraft version.
  NEOFORGE_VERSION="$(echo "${NEOFORGE_VERSION:-}" | tr -d ' ')"

  if [[ -n ${NEOFORGE_VERSION} ]]; then
    # The 1.20.1 release lives in a different repository and is called "forge"
    if [[ "${NEOFORGE_VERSION}" =~ "1.20.1-" ]]; then
      download_link=https://maven.neoforged.net/releases/net/neoforged/forge/${NEOFORGE_VERSION}/forge-${NEOFORGE_VERSION}
      artifact_name="forge"
    else
      download_link=https://maven.neoforged.net/releases/net/neoforged/neoforge/${NEOFORGE_VERSION}/neoforge-${NEOFORGE_VERSION}
      artifact_name="neoforge"
    fi
  else
    # Downloading by Minecraft version means reading the Maven metadata. 1.20.1 is
    # again special: different repository, artifact named "forge" not "neoforge".
    if [[ "${MC_VERSION}" == "1.20.1" ]]; then
      xml_data=$(curl -sSL https://maven.neoforged.net/releases/net/neoforged/forge/maven-metadata.xml)
      artifact_name="forge"
      neoforge_old=1
    else
      xml_data=$(curl -sSL https://maven.neoforged.net/releases/net/neoforged/neoforge/maven-metadata.xml)
      artifact_name="neoforge"
    fi

    repo_url="https://maven.neoforged.net/releases/net/neoforged/${artifact_name}/"

    # Upstream reads these two elements with `xq`. This image has no xq, and
    # apt-installing one to read a flat document is not worth the install-time
    # network dependency, so grep/sed it is.
    if [[ "${MC_VERSION}" == "latest" ]] || [[ -z "${MC_VERSION}" ]]; then
      echo "Getting the latest version of NeoForge."
      neo_release=$(printf '%s' "$xml_data" | grep -oE '<release>[^<]+</release>' | sed -E 's|</?release>||g' | tail -n1)
      MC_VERSION="1.$(echo "$neo_release" | cut -d'.' -f1-2)"
    fi

    echo "Minecraft version: ${MC_VERSION}"

    if [[ -z "${neoforge_old}" ]]; then
      # Modern artifacts drop the leading "1." from the Minecraft version
      version_key=$(echo -n "${MC_VERSION}" | cut -d'.' -f2-)
    else
      # 1.20.1 uses Forge's naming scheme, so just append a dash
      version_key="${MC_VERSION}-"
    fi

    # Literal prefix match — the same semantics as upstream's XPath starts-with(),
    # without regex metacharacters in the version turning into wildcards.
    NEOFORGE_VERSION=$(printf '%s' "$xml_data" \
      | grep -oE '<version>[^<]+</version>' \
      | sed -E 's|</?version>||g' \
      | while read -r candidate; do [[ $candidate == "${version_key}"* ]] && echo "$candidate"; done \
      | tail -n1)

    if [[ -z "${NEOFORGE_VERSION}" ]]; then
      echo "The install failed because there is no valid version of NeoForge for the version of Minecraft selected."
      exit 1
    fi

    echo "NeoForge version: ${NEOFORGE_VERSION}"

    download_link="${repo_url}${NEOFORGE_VERSION}/${artifact_name}-${NEOFORGE_VERSION}"
  fi

  echo "Downloading NeoForge version ${NEOFORGE_VERSION}"
  echo "Download link is ${download_link}"

  if ! curl --output /dev/null --silent --head --fail "${download_link}-installer.jar"; then
    echo "Installer link is invalid. Exiting now."
    exit 2
  fi

  curl -sS -o installer.jar "${download_link}-installer.jar"

  if [[ ! -f ./installer.jar ]]; then
    echo "!!! Error downloading NeoForge version ${NEOFORGE_VERSION} !!!"
    exit 3
  fi

  # Delete args to support downgrading/upgrading
  rm -rf libraries/net/neoforged/${artifact_name}
  rm -f unix_args.txt

  echo "Installing NeoForge server."
  java -jar installer.jar --installServer || {
    echo ""
    echo "Install failed using NeoForge version ${NEOFORGE_VERSION} and Minecraft version ${MC_VERSION}."
    echo "If the server has an unlimited (0) memory value, raise the default install resource limits in the Wings config, or set an explicit memory value in the server's Build Configuration — otherwise the NeoForge installer has no memory to work with."
    exit 4
  }

  # Same fixed path as the forge branch, so one startup command serves both.
  ln -sf libraries/net/neoforged/${artifact_name}/*/unix_args.txt unix_args.txt

  echo "Deleting installer.jar file."
  rm -rf installer.jar
}

case "${SOFTWARE}" in
  purpur)
    install_purpur
    ;;
  fabric)
    install_fabric
    ;;
  forge)
    install_forge
    ;;
  neoforge)
    install_neoforge
    ;;
  *)
    echo "Unknown MC_SOFTWARE '${SOFTWARE}'. Expected one of: purpur, fabric, forge, neoforge."
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

default_server_properties

echo "Installation of ${SOFTWARE} is complete."

variables.name: Build Number
variables.description: The Purpur build to install. Ignored by Fabric, Forge and NeoForge, which always install the promoted build for the selected Minecraft version.

variables.name: Server Software
variables.description: Which Minecraft server software to install. Set by the storefront from the type chosen at creation and not editable afterwards, because changing it would desync the startup command from the installed files.

variables.name: Minecraft Version
variables.description: The version of Minecraft to install. Leave at "latest" to always get the newest release. For Fabric, "snapshot" is also accepted.

variables.name: Server Jar File
variables.description: The name of the jar file to run the server with.
